description: Per-repo Renovate config, processed by the maintainer's self-hosted runner.
hassette-client is pinned twice: in manifest.json (what HA installs) and in the test dependency group (what CI tests). One grouped PR bumps both; tests/test_manifest.py fails if they drift.
The HA-floor CI job pins its own pytest-homeassistant-custom-component in tests.yml, outside Renovate's reach on purpose: the floor moves only when the code needs a newer HA, together with hacs.json.

Non-major updates automerge through GitHub auto-merge once the required checks pass, after minimumReleaseAge holds each release for 3 days (timestamp-optional, so Action digests without a release timestamp aren't held forever). Major updates also automerge for dev tooling only (dependency-groups, GitHub Actions): if one breaks, CI fails and the autofix reviewer picks it up. Majors of runtime dependencies (hassette-client in manifest.json) never automerge.

customManagers tracks each GitHub-hosted hook repo's rev in prek.toml against its tags: Renovate's built-in pre-commit manager only reads .pre-commit-config.yaml, so prek.toml pins would otherwise go stale silently.

customManagers.description: prek.toml hook repo revs (each `repo = "https://github.com/..."` line followed directly by its `rev = ...` line)

packageRules.description: Skip Adoptium respins (OpenJDK x.y.z.N+b). Adoptium's API folds the fourth version part into the semver build (25.0.5.1+2 becomes 25.0.5+100000002), and Renovate writes that string into mise.toml, but mise names the build temurin-25.0.5.1+2.0.LTS and can't install the folded name. Writing the four-part name by hand doesn't work either: it isn't valid semver, so Renovate stops tracking java. Regular releases have small build numbers; a three-plus-digit build is a folded respin, with or without the .LTS suffix (non-LTS versions have none).
Automerge non-major updates once the required checks pass
Automerge major updates of dev tooling once the required checks pass; runtime dependency majors stay manual
A client bump changes what users install, so it is a fix that release-please releases.
Dev and CI dependencies don't reach users and stay out of the changelog.
prek tooling: every hook rev in prek.toml moves together
prek tooling: the prek CLI (mise.toml) and its GitHub Action join the hook revs

Python follows Home Assistant's supported version, so only patch bumps happen. After every automerge rule so it wins. matchDepNames, not matchPackageNames: the package names are python/cpython (mise) and actions/python-versions (setup-python).
